The Government will review all questions received but is not obligated to answer questions submitted after the date noted above, prior to IFB close.

title: JTRS Ground Adaptor Kit
description: ADM(MAT), on behalf of the RCAF, has identified a requirement to procure commercially available power supplies, rack-mount cooling equipment, and factory-terminated cabling to support the operation of JTRS Platform I radios in fixed-site Link 16 operational and training environments. The purpose of this procurement is to enable JTRS Platform I radios to operate outside pre-integrated rack solutions by providing the necessary ancillary hardware for power distribution, thermal management, and external connectivity, without including installation, system integration, testing, or certification. JTRS Platform I radios require external DC power conversion, forced-air cooling capable of supporting both the radio and its associated power supply in a single 19-inch rack, and standardized power, data/control, and human-machine interface cabling manufactured in accordance with recognized military and aerospace construction practices. Some required cable assemblies rely on controlled U.S. Government interface specifications, limiting eligible suppliers to those with existing authorization. The procurement also includes external rack-mountable DC power supplies capable of delivering nominal 280 VDC at continuous duty and rack-compatible multi-fan cooling assemblies rated for sustained high-power transmission. Deliverables consist of 20 DC power supply units, 20 rack-mount cooling trays, and 20 complete sets of factory-terminated power, data/control, timing, and HMIG cables as defined in the specification. To be delivered to Unit #3 1941 Robertson Road Bells Corners, Nepean Ottawa ON K2H 5B7.

title: Joinery Contractors Framework
description: NHS Lanarkshire Health Board (“the Board”) invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for appointment to the NHSL329-26 Joinery Contractors Framework. The framework will support the Property & Support Services Division in delivering planned, reactive, routine and emergency joinery works across NHS Lanarkshire’s healthcare estate. The framework will comprise three lots: Lot 1: University Hospital Monklands, works below GBP 5,000 - Lot 1 covers planned, routine, reactive and emergency joinery works valued below GBP 5,000 at University Hospital Monklands. One contractor will be appointed and must provide a responsive service, including 24-hour, 365-day emergency cover, in accordance with the specified priority response times. Lot 2: Community Sites, works below GBP 5,000 - Lot 2 covers planned, routine, reactive and emergency joinery works valued below GBP 5,000 across the NHS Lanarkshire community sites listed in Appendix A of the Specification. One contractor will be appointed and must provide a responsive service, including 24-hour, 365-day emergency cover and travel between sites where required. Lot 3: Small Works valued between GBP 5,000 and GBP 50,000 - Lot 3 covers planned joinery works valued over GBP 5,000 and up to GBP 50,000. Between three and five contractors may be appointed, comprising Primary and Reserve Contractors. Requirements will normally be awarded through quotation or mini-competition, with the applicable award criteria and quality-to-price weighting confirmed for each requirement. The framework will operate for an initial period of 24 months, with the option to extend for a further two 12-month periods. Contractors must provide a safe, reliable and responsive service that supports clinical operations.

title: Protein ENGineering (PENG)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for the development of a multifunctional, target-agnostic platform for precise, programmable editing of endogenous proteins. The goal of the Protein ENGineering (PENG) program is to transition proteome engineering from a collection of isolated, bespoke tools into a universal, software-defined discipline. The PENG program will establish a comprehensive, integrated platform composed of modular targeting, generalizable effector chemistries, and multiplexed control systems. Rather than developing isolated, target-specific tools, performers will integrate novel splicing, ligation, and co-translational techniques to directly recognize, modify, and rewrite endogenous proteins within complex biological architectures. Performers may explore multiple technical paths, progressively advancing their approaches from foundational validation to robust demonstrations of efficacy. Ultimately, this integrated platform will be validated in high-fidelity cellular models (e.g., organoids), to provide an integrated proof-of-concept at the tissue level.

title: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA): Cost Estimating Modeling Data, Analytics Research (CEMDAR)
description: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Closed Two-Step BAA: SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) The Two-Step Process reduces acquisition resources for both the Government and industry. It may be considered when a large number of proposals are anticipated or to determine if further Government interest is warranted. If further interest is not warranted, industry saves unnecessary bid and proposal costs and the Government saves review time. Broad Agency Announcement Number FA7014-26-S-CS02 Announcement Title SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) Federal Agency Name Secretary of the Air Force Financial Management (SAF/FM) Announcement Type & Acquisition Set-Aside Initial Announcement | 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code & Size Standard 541745 (Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees) Estimated Program Ceiling $24,000,000 (Anticipated Awards: 1 single award) White Paper Submission Deadline October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time 1. Overview Information & Two-Step Solicitation Structure SAF/FM is soliciting white papers on the research effort described herein. White papers must be addressed to the Contracting Points of Contact (POCs). This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 541745. White papers and resultant proposals submitted shall strictly comply with this announcement. There will be no separate formal solicitation issued regarding this requirement. This BAA will be republished at yearly intervals for administrative updates and ease of reference. 1.1 Two-Step Acquisition Sequence Step 1 � White Paper Due Date & Submission: White papers may be electronically submitted upon issuance of this BAA until October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time. Only white papers are accepted at this stage. Submissions must be delivered electronically to AFDW/PK at eric.moss.3@us.af.mil and joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil. Step 2 � Formal Proposal Due Date & Time: Formal technical and cost proposals will be requested solely from offerors whose submitted white papers are evaluated as successfully meeting the operational and research needs of the Air Force. Late Receipt Provisions: White paper and proposal receipts after the specified cutoff date and time shall be governed strictly by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). 1.2 Instrument Types and Contracting Guidance The Air Force reserves the right to award the contractual instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype authority, Grant, Cooperative Agreement, OT for Research, or an applicable technology transfer mechanism. Awards under this BAA are generally anticipated to be cost-reimbursement. Offerors are specifically advised that cost-reimbursement contracts require an accounting system determined adequate by the Government for tracking allocable contract costs. 1.3 Communications & Contracting Points of Contact Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged prior to proposal submission. Technical discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to fund or award any proposed effort. Only warranted Contracting Officers possess the legal authority to commit the Government. Inquiries regarding this solicitation should be directed to the Contracting POCs: Primary Contracting Officer: Eric Moss � eric.moss.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Joseph Spear � joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil 2. Section I � Program Description & Strategic Objectives The Department of the Air Force (DAF) has identified critical operational gaps in the enterprise databases, analytical methods, and predictive tools regularly employed for weapon system cost estimating and analysis. DAF is actively committed to modernizing the efficiency, fidelity, and throughput of its cost estimating capabilities. This requirement invests in strengthening, accelerating, and elevating cost data and analytic capabilities using modern data science and cloud engineering technologies to enable faster, higher-quality, and higher-volume analytic decision support across the DAF cost community. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. title: Two Phase Design and Construction of the Port Monmouth Phase II, Contract 1 Mitigation Project
description: As of 18 September 2026: RTA 30% Package broken up and uploaded due to SAM size limitation. As of 17 September 2026: Phase I of a Two Phase BVTO posted. The Port Monmouth project consists of shore protection components (Phase 1) as well as flood risk management components (Phase II). The project provides for reduction of storm damages to low-lying residential and commercial structures from coastal erosion, tidal flooding, and inland flooding along Pews and Compton Creeks caused by high surface events in Raritan Bay. Phase II flood risk management components consist of a tide gate, levees, floodwalls, two pump stations, three road closure structures, road raising and regarding, and wetland mitigation. The State of New Jersey, acting through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), is the non-Federal sponsor for the project.

title: Two Phase Design and Construction of the Port Monmouth Phase II, Contract 1 Mitigation Project
description: As of 18 September 2026: RTA 30% Package broken up and uploaded due to SAM size limitation. As of 17 September 2026: Phase I of a Two Phase BVTO posted. The Port Monmouth project consists of shore protection components (Phase 1) as well as flood risk management components (Phase II). The project provides for reduction of storm damages to low-lying residential and commercial structures from coastal erosion, tidal flooding, and inland flooding along Pews and Compton Creeks caused by high surface events in Raritan Bay. Phase II flood risk management components consist of a tide gate, levees, floodwalls, two pump stations, three road closure structures, road raising and regarding, and wetland mitigation. The State of New Jersey, acting through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), is the non-Federal sponsor for the project.

title: Two Phase Design and Construction of the Port Monmouth Phase II, Contract 1 Mitigation Project
description: As of 17 September 2026: Phase I of a Two Phase BVTO posted. The Port Monmouth project consists of shore protection components (Phase 1) as well as flood risk management components (Phase II). The project provides for reduction of storm damages to low-lying residential and commercial structures from coastal erosion, tidal flooding, and inland flooding along Pews and Compton Creeks caused by high surface events in Raritan Bay. Phase II flood risk management components consist of a tide gate, levees, floodwalls, two pump stations, three road closure structures, road raising and regarding, and wetland mitigation. The State of New Jersey, acting through the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP), is the non-Federal sponsor for the project.

title: Z2DA--589A7-23-306 Renovate Bldg. 5 & 5B for Mental Health FY27 NRM
description: Contractor shall perform construction and renovation of the existing space in Building 5 &/or 5B at the Robert J. Dole VA Medical Center campus. This project will prepare approximately 1,100 SF of existing space in building 5 and/or 5B for use as a same day access mental health clinic in adherence to VHA directive 1231(2) & VHA Handbook 1160.1. This project shall be executed in a manner, following the sequence defined in the design narrative, to maintain continuous operations of adjacent VA clinical functions and medical center functionality throughout construction. All construction work shall be performed in full compliance with the complete set of bidding documents, including all contract drawings, specifications, and design narratives associated with this solicitation necessary to convert the existing space into four exam rooms, a combined waiting/reception area, a relocated police office, and associated support spaces. The general contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to execute the required scope of work. Construction will consist of, but is not limited to, the following: � Selective demolition of existing interior partitions, ceilings, finishes, and elements required for new clinic layout. � Installation of new interior finishes including flooring, wall finishes, ceilings, trim, and casework. � Implementation of therapeutic design features, including calm color schemes, anchored artwork, secure hardware, and achieving a minimum STC-45 acoustic rating for exam room partitions. � Installation of new wall-mounted lavatories in each exam room. Routing new domestic hot and cold water from adjacent restrooms and trenching new water lines across the corridor to existing tin-in points. � Rebalancing and modifying HVAC systems; reusing the existing rooftop AHU serving the building; relocating or adding diffusers/grilles; installing ligature-resistant diffusers in exam rooms � Providing new electrical receptacles, data outlets, and circuits to support clinical functions � Installing LED lighting including secured, ligature-resistant fixtures in exam rooms; relocating or supplementing lighting in general spaces; adding occupancy sensors. � Removal of existing sprinklers, providing temporary upright sprinkler coverage during construction, and installing new sprinklers to meet NFPA 13 standards Statement of Work for Project 589A7-23-306, Renovate 5 & 5B for Mental Health July 08, 2026 2 � Site preparation for installation of Government?furnished equipment, including structural supports, utility connections, and required interfaces. � Hazardous materials abatement, including asbestos remediation in areas identified during construction; asbestos?containing materials are expected in some work areas and must be removed or handled per applicable VA, EPA, OSHA, and state/local regulations. � All other items as described in the contract documents. This construction work is located in an occupied, operational clinical facility and must be performed in a manner that allows medical care services to continue uninterrupted throughout construction, This requires carefully phased construction, strict adherence to ICRA, infection control, noise/vibration limits, and daily coordination with the VA COR and end users. Construction may also include the abatement of any asbestos as identified on the provided drawings. The construction of this project will take place in a very busy occupied building and is to be completed to allow medical care functions to be maintained uninterrupted throughout construction � necessitating carefully phased construction and coordination with VA COR/users, including strict adherence to ICRA requirements.

title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YRBM-50
description: 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L. ________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. description: 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L.____________________The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. title: AN/BYG-1 Applications
description: Description SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. Consolidated Access Request Instructions Prospective Offerors must submit a single, consolidated access request email to the Points of Contact listed below to obtain E-TIC portal access and the classified GFI software package. Email Attachments Required: DD Form 254: A completed copy of the DD Form 254. Block 6 must verify that the requesting company possesses a Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) issued SECRET facility clearance (FCL) and SECRET safeguarding capability. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTE FOR AWARD ELIGIBILITY: While a SECRET FCL is sufficient for proposal preparation and GFI access, the Offeror must ultimately possess a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET facility clearance and TOP SECRET safeguarding capability, issued by the U.S. Government, no later than contract award. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. DD Form 2345: A current, approved copy of the company�s DD Form 2345 (Military Critical Technical Data Agreement). Executed Terms of Use Agreement (TOUA): A signed copy of the TOUA, executed by the Offeror's Facility Security Officer (FSO) or authorized corporate representative. Email Body Requirements: Subject Line: Format as N00024-26-R-6222 Access Request - [Insert Company Name]. Company Info: Provide the Company Name and active CAGE Code. E-TIC Representative: Provide the full name, official company email address, and phone number of the designated individual who will serve as the E-TIC account holder. Classified Media Request (Yes/No): State explicitly whether your company is requesting delivery of the classified software source code. Classified Mailing Info (Required only if requesting Classified Media): Provide the name and contact information of the company's FSO, along with the verified Classified Mailing Address of your facility as registered in the National Industrial Security System (NISS). If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. E-TIC Portal Registration (Unclassified/CUI Documents) Once the Government approves the consolidated request, the designated E-TIC representative must complete their account setup on the AIMTC portal. Access requires a DoD Common Access Card (CAC) or an approved DoD External Certification Authority (ECA) Certificate, along with an active Joint Certification Program (JCP) registration number. For New AIMTC Account Requests: Visit https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil and complete the AIMTC Account Request Form. For Existing AIMTC Account Holders: Log into https://aimtc.nuwc.navy.mil, click �My Profile�, and update your fields exactly as follows: Name: First name, middle initial, last name. Foreign National: Select "Yes" or "No". Email Address: Official company email only (no Gmail, Yahoo, etc.). Branch or Code: PMS425 Phone Number: Requestor's direct phone number. NUWC Sponsor POC: Eun-Ja O. Rau NUWC Sponsor Code: PMS425 Justification: "Prospective Offeror for the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications" Scroll down, expand �E-TIC (Electronic Technical Information Center)�, select "BYG-1 Applications Solicitation", provide your justification, and click �Send.� For AIMTC account issues, contact AIMTC_Webmaster@us.navy.mil. Please note that you will not be able to access the PMS425 AN/BYG-1 Applications until your account request is approved by the Approval Official and processed. Please allow for processing. If E-TIC access has not been granted within five (5) business days of your initial email package submission, please contact the Points of Contact listed below for status. The proposal due date will not be extended due to late or incomplete access requests. Over the course of the procurement, the Government may provide E-TIC updates or additional materials to the same designated company representative. Transmission of Classified Media (Software Code) Upon successful verification of the Offeror's FCL, safeguarding capabilities, and NISS mailing address provided in the consolidated email request, and formal approval of the Offeror's E-TIC access (including receipt of the executed TOUA and approved DD Form 2345), the Government will package and transmit the classified media in strict accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM). title: USACE - Industry Day 2026
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Middle East District, will host an in-person and virtual Industry Day on 22 October 2026. Check-in on the day of the event will begin at 0730. Tentative agenda will include a Contracting and Programs overview along with a focused session on the upcoming Qatar Development of Al Udeid (QDA) program and an upcoming Space Campus project that is anticipated to be awarded via a new delivery method called Integrated Design and Construction (IDaC). There will be an opportunity for breakout sessions and a question & answer (Q&A) session with Contracting, Construction, Engineering, and Programs and Project Management. The location will be the DoubleTree by Hilton, Blue Ridge Shadows, 111 Hospitality Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630. The purpose of Industry Day is for our architect-engineer and general contractor partners to have a glimpse of the current and upcoming program opportunities in the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR) to allow both USACE and our contractor community to be better prepared for the work ahead. There will be an opportunity to openly discuss any questions, comments, concerns, and best practices contractors have about working in the CENTCOM AOR during the Q&A session. The Middle East District will solicit questions from industry in advance of the event. Please submit any questions by 1600 Eastern Daylight Time, 16 October 2025 to the attention of Jeanette Farrell at Jeanette.M.Farrell@usace.army.mil, with the Subject Line: Industry Day Oct 2026. Questions will be evaluated, and responses provided during the Q&A portion of the event. All attendees are required to register online to provide their company name and attendee names with titles by 19 October 2026. For questions regarding this event, please feel free to contact Jeanette Farrell at the email address shown above.

description: Solicitation Notice: 36C79126R0011 � Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program Notice Type: Solicitation Issuance Notice Solicitation Number: 36C79126R0011 Posted Date: September 18, 2026 Response Due Date: October 19, 2026, 3:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) NAICS Code: 334510 � Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). This tiered evaluation methodology is authorized under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and implemented through the VA�s Class Deviation to VAAR 815.101?370, which permits the use of tiered set?aside procedures to minimize procurement delays in situations where market research indicates that award at the SDVOSB or VOSB tiers is uncertain. Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is pleased to announce the release of Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011, the official Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. Key Dates: RFP Questions Due-In Date: On or before but no later than October 5, 2026, at 3:00 PM CDT, questions received after this deadline may receive a Government response or receipt acknowledgement. The VA reserves the right not to make an award or to make award on some CLINs/SLINs but not all the CLINs/SLINs enumerated in the solicitation. title: USACE - Industry Day 2026
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Middle East District, will host an in-person and virtual Industry Day on 22 October 2026. Check-in on the day of the event will begin at 0730. Tentative agenda will include a Contracting and Programs overview and a focused session on the Qatar Development Area Space Campus. There will be an opportunity for breakout sessions and a question & answer (Q&A) session with Contracting, Construction, Engineering, and Programs and Project Management. The location will be the DoubleTree by Hilton, Blue Ridge Shadows, 111 Hospitality Drive, Front Royal, VA 22630. The purpose of Industry Day is for our architect-engineer and general contractor partners to have a glimpse of the current and upcoming program opportunities in the CENTCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR) to allow both USACE and our contractor community to be better prepared for the work ahead. There will be an opportunity to openly discuss any questions, comments, concerns, and best practices contractors have about working in the CENTCOM AOR during the Q&A session. The Middle East District will solicit questions from industry in advance of the event. Please submit any questions by 1600 Eastern Daylight Time, 16 October 2025 to the attention of Jeanette Farrell at Jeanette.M.Farrell@usace.army.mil, with the Subject Line: Industry Day Oct 2026. Questions will be evaluated, and responses provided during the Q&A portion of the event. All attendees are required to register online to provide their company name and attendee names with titles by 19 October 2026. Please register using the following hyperlink: https://events.dod.teams.microsoft.us/event/e963de64-91e6-4c99-9f20-cf582117491c@fc4d76ba-f17c-4c50-b9a7-8f3163d27582?source=copyLinkLegacyShareLinkDialog When entering the meeting via MS Teams, please enter as a guest utilizing the email provided during registration. We are currently not limiting in-person attendance at the event; however, this may change if an overwhelming number of companies intend to send representatives. A questionnaire is included for the submittal with RSVP. There is no cost to attend this event. Presentation slides will be provided prior to the event. For questions regarding this event, please feel free to contact Jeanette Farrell at the email address shown above.

description: Description NOTE: On 8 August 2026, Solicitation Amendment 001 was published in the E-TIC portal, including a revised solicitation, a revised Section L, and a Question & Answer set Batch 1. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. description: Solicitation Notice: 36C79126R0011 � Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program Notice Type: Solicitation Issuance Notice Solicitation Number: 36C79126R0011 Posted Date: September 18, 2026 Response Due Date: October 19, 2026, 3:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) NAICS Code: 334510 � Electromedical and Electrotherapeutic Apparatus Manufacturing. The Small Business size standard for NAICS Code 334510 is 1,250 employees. This NAICS code is appropriate as it encompasses the manufacturing of FDA?regulated electromedical therapeutic equipment including TENS, IFC, neuromodulation, and diathermy devices. PSC: 6515 � Medical and Surgical Instruments, Equipment, and Supplies Set-Aside: The Tiered Set-Aside Evaluation Approach used by the VA is not classified as a traditional Small Business set-aside, but rather as a competitive negotiated procurement, conducted via a tiered evaluation process aimed at prioritizing award to successive small business categories. This acquisition will be conducted using the VA Tiered Set?Aside Evaluation Approach pursuant to the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8127, including the statutory priority ordering prescribed in 38 U.S.C. �?8127(h) (a subsection of the Veterans First Contracting Program statute) and the procedures outlined in Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Under this approach, the Government will solicit offers from all tiers of Offerors simultaneously; however, proposal evaluations and award determination will occur sequentially in the prescribed order of priority. The tiers for this procurement are as follows: Tier-1 Service?Disabled Veteran?Owned Small Business (SDVOSB): SDVOSBs shall be evaluated first in accordance with VA�s statutory obligation to prioritize verified SDVOSBs when the VA Rule of Two is met. If no award can be made at Tier-1, then verified VOSB offers will be evaluated next in Tier-2, consistent with the Veterans First hierarchy. Tier-2 Veteran?Owned Small Business (VOSB): If no award can be made at Tier 2, the Government will evaluate offers from all other eligible small business concerns, (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, and WOSB are considered before considering other small business concerns), in Tier 3 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101-3 and VAAR 815.101-370 (Class Deviation). Tier-3 Other Small Business Concerns: If no award can be made at Tier-3, the Government will evaluate offers from all Other-Than-Small-Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses)) in Tier 4 following the tiering procedures established in VAAR 815.101?3 and 815.101?370 (Class Deviation). Tier-4 Other?Than?Small Business (OTSB) Concerns (Large Businesses): If no award can be made under any small business Tier 1 through 3, the Government will evaluate offers from other?than?small businesses or large business concerns in Tier 4. This tiered evaluation methodology is authorized under 38 U.S.C. 8127 and implemented through the VA�s Class Deviation to VAAR 815.101?370, which permits the use of tiered set?aside procedures to minimize procurement delays in situations where market research indicates that award at the SDVOSB or VOSB tiers is uncertain. Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs, Enterprise Procurement Office, Acquisition Service Four Delta Team, 555 Corporate Circle, Golden, CO 80401-5621. Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is pleased to announce the release of Solicitation Number 36C79126R0011, the official Request for Proposals (RFP) for the Electro-Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The objective of this national procurement program is to establish multiple single-awards of Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Base contracts and resultant FFP/IDIQ Delivery Order contracts to be awarded on a per-Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) and per-Sub-Line Item Number (SLIN) basis for the procurement of FDA-cleared electro-therapeutic devices and accessories supporting non-opioid pain management for Veterans across all VA Medical Centers and Community-Based Outpatient Clinics. This solicitation recompetition of the expiring legacy TENS contract and expands the legacy TENS procurement program to include Interferential Current Therapy (IFC) devices, Short-Wave Diathermy (SWD) devices (thermal and non-thermal), and portable Neuromodulation systems - for the treatment of headache disorders to be inclusive all unique parent CLIN devices and the device accessories has enumerated at the discrete subordinate SLINs. The device accessories categorized as SLINs include but are not limited to electrodes, lead wires, power chargers, garment-based applicators, and associated other consumables. Each product of the ETMPM-TENS requirement is mapped to unique parent CLIN and a discrete subordinate SLINs with universal Minimum Technical Requirements (MTRs) applicable to all CLINs/SLINs and individual CLIN/SLIN-specific MTRs. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. REQUIREMENTS GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall provide at the contractors facility the necessary repair labor, new and serviceable reworked repair parts, materials and test equipmentand arrange for outside services as required to return the equipment to a serviceable condition within the calendar day shop time as specified in the delivery schedule of the contract. SCOPE OF WORK FOR REPAIR: The scope of the work in the following subparagraphs are applicable to the latest configuration of the Government equipment.There shall be a 100% repair rate on all CLIN carcasses. Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. In the event that the failed assembly is found to be beyond economical repair (BER), as defined in the contract, or in the event that the Government equipment is received with one or more subassemblies missing (FOR EXAMPLE: AS ARESULT OF CANNABALIZATION BY AN AIRCRAFT OPERATING SITE),the contractor shall promptly obtain confirmation of such findings from the cognizant DCMC QAR. and upon confirmation promptly notify the PCO for authority to scrap if BER and,if missing subassemblies, proceed IAW Missing on Induction (MOI).Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing parts are received or unless specifically authorized by the PCO. All disassembly, repair and assembly of the Government equipment shall be IAW current engineering drawings and configuration specifications. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Replaced hardware shall be in accordance with the latest drawing revisions.The contractor shall provide and may use new or repaired/reworked parts which meet the requirements of the repair specification to restore the Government equipment in the delivery time specified in the contract. Repaired/reworked parts shall be used in lieu of new whenever possible as allowed by the applicable repair specification.Any repair of lower assemblies and/or detail parts not authorized by the by the applicable repair specification shall be submitted to the QAR for Government review and approval.Requests for repair approvals shall be accompanied by details of the repair and other applicable data such as tests which have been performed to validate the repair. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REPAIR PARTS: The contractor shall be responsible for identification, selection, ordering, and stocking of required piece parts to support all repairs. By definition," piece part" shall be any part or material listed in the applicable repair specification. TEST EQUIPMENT: The contractor will provide a laboratory facility equipped with instrumentation and testing capability for comprehensive functional testing of the equipment and detailed inspections of subassemblies and detailed parts. The contractor test equipment shall be designed to ensure repaired Government equipment function in full compliance with the requirementsof the applicable repair specification. All Government equipment's electrical performance and mechanical parameters shall be measured in accordance with the requirements of the applicable repair specification,with hard copy reports of all measurements available to the Government upon request. description: Предметът и обемът на обществената поръчка включва изпълнението на следните дейности: 1. Основна дейност 1: „Развитие на Институционална архитектура на АМ по отношение на Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа (СУИД)“; 2. Основна дейност 2: „Въвеждане на Институционалната архитектура на Агенция „Митници“ по отношение на Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа (СУИД)“, чрез: Надградена 1 бр. Система за управление на идентичностите и достъпа в съответствие със съюзните функционални изисквания, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8; Реализирана 1 бр. интеграция на СУИД със Системата за директен достъп на търговците до европейските ИС UUM&DS, Release 2.8; Актуализирани версии на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) до последните актуални версии, издадени от производителя и реинженеринг на СУИД при необходимост; Актуализирани, при необходимост 2 бр. спецификации, свързани със СУИД, във връзка с изискванията, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8, последните актуални версии на готовите решения на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) и надграждане на съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД; Надградени съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД; Запазени съществуващи интеграции на СУИД с митническите информационни системи, националните регистри (Търговски регистър, Регистър Булстат, Регистър Национална база данни „Население“ и Регистър Единен регистър на чужденците) и RegiX, и при необходимост надграждане на интеграциите с изискванията, произтичащи от UUM&DS, Release 2.8, последните актуални версии на готовите решения на OpenText Identity Manager 25.4 (NetIQ Identity Manager 4.10.2) и OpenText Access Manager 25.3 (NetIQ Access Manager 5.1.2) и надграждане на съществуващи работни процеси (workflows) и функционалности на СУИД. 3. Основна дейност 3: „Обучение на 50 служители на АМ (10 приложни администратори, 5 системни администратори, 5 потребители за регистрации на ИО в Е-Портала на АМ и 30 потребители с права на ръководител) за работа с реализираните функционалности по дейността“.

Consumables are outlined in Attachment B. Work Hours / Load Bank Testing Section 4.3 identifies the monthly PM for the two 600 kW generators and one 500 kW generator as occurring on the second Tuesday of each month from 4:00 AM to 7:00 AM, while the 1250 kW and 750 kW generators may be serviced during normal business hours. Please confirm whether the annual load-bank testing, ATS maintenance, sampling, and other annual maintenance activities may also be performed during normal business hours unless otherwise coordinated with the COR. The 600 s, and 500 are backing up a critical production line that is old and has issues during power transfers. We require them and their associated equipment to be cycled or maintained prior to that department s workday start, so they can start the production line on time with no delay. This department is the Consolidated Mail Order Pharmacy (CMOP). All the generator maintenance is to be performed on the second Tuesday of each month, we need the CMOP Generators started and done first. Transformer Annual Inspection and IR Scan The scope includes quarterly energized transformer inspections as well as an annual inspection that includes additional maintenance activities and an IR scan. The pricing schedule only provides a quarterly transformer CLIN with a quantity of four. Please confirm whether the annual transformer inspection and IR scan are to be included within the pricing for the four quarterly inspections, with one quarterly service incorporating the annual work, or if the annual service is to be priced separately. Please confirm the intended operating condition for the annual IR scan, as it appears under the annual de-energized inspection section. Annual Transformer and ATS IR Scanning Procedure The annual infrared (IR) scan of transformer lugs and automatic transfer switches (ATSs) is to be completed while the equipment is energized, prior to any deenergizing procedures. This approach allows for the identification of potential faults under operating conditions, ensuring that any issues are detected before maintenance begins. Once the IR scan is performed, any necessary repairs should be made during the scheduled deenergized maintenance period. This ensures that faults identified during the scan can be addressed safely while the equipment is not under load. The IR scan should occur once each year and, whenever possible, should be scheduled close to the time of the annual deenergized maintenance. This coordination facilitates efficient fault resolution and minimizes downtime. In the event of an emergent issue identified during the scan, immediate corrective action will be taken to address the problem as soon as possible, regardless of the scheduled maintenance cycle.

title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production
description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO�s and TDPs.

title: Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain. The Assignment will align with and leverage the resulting business, data, application, technology and security architectures to guide the design and implementation of WRIMS, while supporting the operationalisation of the EA, particularly in systems integration, interoperability, data governance, ICT infrastructure and cybersecurity. The Assignment is divided into three phases: Phase I: Detailed verification, system analysis and preparation Phase II: A Kenyan-led option assessment and decision Phase III: Design, build, test, roll-out and stabilised operation

Diese werden auf zwei separaten, nicht miteinander verbundenen Baufeldern auf der Liegenschaft erstellt. Die Erschließung erfolgt über das Haupttor der Kaserne. Die Flächen sind verkehrstechnisch über die befestigten Straßenflächen innerhalb des Geländes erschlossen. Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 47 soll auf einer ehemaligen Waldfläche an der südöstlichen Grenze des Geländes realisiert werden. Das Grundstück wird im Rahmen des Bauvorhabens an die bestehende Infrastruktur der Liegenschaft angeschlossen. Das Baufeld umfasst ca. 5.860m². Der Neubau des Unterkunftsgebäudes 54 ist auf der Fläche zwischen den Gebäuden 53 und der RÜH (Rettungsübungshalle) geplant. title: Zambia – Water pumps – Bau von Solar-PV-Stromerzeugungssystemen und Austausch und Sanierung von Pumpensystemen
description: Das Projekt „Nexus Energy Water Programme for Zambia“ (NEWZA) zielt darauf ab, die Verflechtung zwischen dem Energie- und dem Wassersektor zu stärken. Das Projekt wird von der Europäischen Union (EU) und dem Bundesministerium für wirtschaftliche Zusammenarbeit und Entwicklung (BMZ) der Bundesrepublik Deutschland über die KfW kofinanziert. Das NEWZA-Programm umfasst auch laufende Projekte, die von der deutschen Bundesregierung kofinanziert werden, nämlich: • Programm „Städtische Wasserversorgung und Abwasserentsorgung in der Ostprovinz, Phase IV“ (BMZ-Nr.: 2016 67 328/2018 67 514/2018 70 104) und • Management von Wasserressourcen und Abwasserentsorgung für mittelgroße Städte (BMZ-Nr.: 2020 67 494, 2022 70 023). Das Ziel von NEWZA ist es, den Zugang zu grüner Energie und Wasserversorgung für alle zu verbessern, indem die Leistungsfähigkeit von fünf sambischen Wasserversorgungsunternehmen gesteigert wird: Southern (Los 1), Chambeshi (Los 2), Lukanga (Los 3), Nkana (Los 4) und Eastern (Los 5). Die Arbeiten werden auf der Grundlage des FIDIC-Vertrags für Anlagen und Design-Build-Verträge, 1. Auflage 1999 (Yellow Book), vergeben. Der Arbeitsumfang für alle kommerziellen Versorgungsunternehmen ist nachstehend aufgeführt. Diese Liste dient lediglich der Veranschaulichung des Umfangs und ist nicht als vollständige Auflistung zu verstehen. Der Arbeitsumfang umfasst: ► Komponente 1 Solar-PV • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Solaranlagen liegen in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das Grundstück für die PV-Anlagen wird entweder innerhalb der Produktions-/Entnahme-/Aufbereitungsanlagen und/oder anderen Standorten der CU bereitgestellt. Reicht die Fläche nicht aus, wird das Grundstück von der CU durch Kauf oder Pacht gesichert • Installation von Online-Überwachungsplattformen für PV-Anlagen, einschließlich Echtzeit-Datenerfassung, -übertragung (GPRS/GSM oder andere), sicherer Cloud-Datenspeicherung und Online-Portalschnittstelle (sicherheitsgeschützt) mit Anzeige der Infrastrukturzustands-/Leistungsdaten auf Standortebene • Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre nach der Planungs- und Bauphase Teilkomponente 1a – Netzgekoppelte Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von netzgekoppelten Solarstromanlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der PV-Anlagen ist durch die Kapazität der vorhandenen Nieder-/Mittelspannungs- und Transformatoranlagen begrenzt. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Verkabelung, Filtern (falls erforderlich), Wechselrichtern, Sammelschienenverlängerungen und Niederspannungsfächern (falls erforderlich). • Durchführung von Standortmessungen der Stromdaten zum Vergleich des Stromverbrauchs vor und nach den Arbeiten. Bei Standorten, an denen Pumpen saniert werden, Bewertung des Anteils des Jahresverbrauchs nach der Pumpensanierung. Teilkomponente 1b – Hybride Solar-PV-Anlagen • Entwurf und Lieferung von hybriden Solar-PV-Anlagen für die bestehenden Wassergewinnungs-/Wasserentnahme-/Wasseraufbereitungsanlagen und/oder andere Standorte der CU. Die Größe der Anlage richtet sich nach der Pumpeneingangsleistung (P1) und der Anzahl der Arbeitspumpen. • An Standorten, an denen Hybridtechnologie zum Einsatz kommt, werden auch die Pumpen und die zugehörigen Stromversorgungsanlagen ausgetauscht. • Dies umfasst die Installation von Solar-PV-Modulen, Anschlusskästen, Filtern (nach Bedarf), Hybrid-Wechselrichtern, Niederspannungsausrüstung für Solar-PV und Pumpen sowie Frequenzumrichtern für Pumpen. Der Umfang der Komponente umfasst die Schnittstelle oder Grenze am Anschlusspunkt für die Kabel von der Niederspannungsausrüstung zu den Pumpen. • Online-Überwachungsplattformen für Standorte, an denen das Hybridsystem in ein einziges System für Pumpen und Solar-PV integriert ist. ► Komponente 2 – Pumpensysteme • Sanierung der bestehenden Pumpensystembeklebung, im Wesentlichen: Pumpen, Kabel, Niederspannungs- und Mittelspannungsschalttafeln, Ventile/Armaturen, Rohrleitungen der Pumpstation, Mess- und Regelgeräte • Projektmanagement, Planung, Installation und Inbetriebnahme der Pumpensysteme in Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers • Das System ist auf gleichbleibende oder erhöhte zukünftige Tagesdurchflussmengen gemäß den Anforderungen der CU ausgelegt. Die täglichen Durchflussmengen und die vorgesehenen Betriebsstunden werden in der Ausschreibung angegeben. • Überprüfung des Betriebsdrucks der Steigleitung durch Tests vor Ort, Ermittlung hydraulischer Probleme (nicht funktionierende Luftventile) und Messung der tatsächlichen Durchflussmengen vor Ort und des Energieverbrauchs der Pumpen (alle Betriebsmodi). Die geschätzten Nennleistungen der Pumpen (Durchfluss, Druck, Nennmotorleistung) werden in der Ausschreibung nur zu Informationszwecken angegeben. Die endgültige Dimensionierung der Pumpen zur Erfüllung der Durchflussanforderungen liegt in der Verantwortung des Auftragnehmers. • Installation eines digitalen Online-Fernüberwachungssystems, das an wichtige Messgeräte (Durchfluss, Druck und Leistung) angeschlossen ist, mit einem 3-Jahres-Abonnement (falls zutreffend) für den Zugang. Keine Fernsteuerung der Systeme. • Technischer Support, Betrieb und Wartung für bis zu 2 Jahre Das Projekt muss in Übereinstimmung mit den KfW-Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinien vorbereitet und durchgeführt werden: https://www.kfw-entwicklungsbank.de/PDF/Download-Center/PDF-Dokumente-Richtlinien/Nachhaltigkeitsrichtlinie_EN.pdf

title: Denmark – Foreign economic-aid-related services – Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya
description: This Assignment is financed from official Danish development assistance through the Danish Africa Water facility (Danish Finance Act § 06.32.01.32). Emphasis is therefore on providing safe and affordable access to water for all (Sustainable Development Goal 6.1), increase water-use efficiency and ensure freshwater supplies (Sustainable Development Goal 6.4) and to raise capacity for planning and management of climate change (Sustainable Goal 13.5). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Royal Danish Embassy, Nairobi (RDE) is the funding agency and Water Resources Authority (WRA) is the Recipient of the outcome of the Assignment. The Assignment aims at operating with a high level of local content by engaging local partners with the view of increasing the long-term sustainability of digital systems and ease of their future maintenance as well as enhanced dialogue on water use with local communities. The Water Resources Authority (WRA) is a state corporation established under Section 11 of the Water Act, 2016 and mandated to regulate the management and use of Kenya's water resources on behalf of the national government. WRA formulates standards and regulations, issues and enforces water permits, sets water-use fees, and advises the Cabinet Secretary on national water-resource policy. WRA operates through a decentralised structure comprising one head office, six basin offices, 26 sub-basins, eight laboratories and three satellite offices. WRA is currently undertaking the development of an Enterprise Architecture as part of the Government’s Digitization of Government Services Performance Contracting initiative, in alignment with the Government Enterprise Architecture framework and applicable Government ICT standards. Kenya has a comparatively clear formal water-resource governance architecture, but implementation is constrained by incomplete coordination across national, basin, county and sub-catchment levels, limited basin and sub-basin resources, and overlapping institutional interfaces. WRA already operates digital permitting, e-billing, smart-metering, hydrological monitoring, GIS and laboratory systems; however, these features remains fragmented and have not yet been demonstrated to provide an end-to-end authoritative record linking the water user and abstraction point to the permit, meter, reading, invoice, payment, inspection and hydrological context. The core information-management challenge is not the absence of digital systems, but their fragmentation across field monitoring, permitting, metering, billing, enforcement and hydrological decision support. WRA is working to create integrations between its various IT solutions, but the vision for this project is to support components in establishing a single point of entry/IT solution—hereinafter referred to as WRIMS—that will ensure integration among all existing IT solutions, as shown in the diagram below and elaborated in the background document on WRA’s existing IT environment. The Assignment regarding Improved Data Collection, Monitoring and Revenue Base for Water Resource Management in Kenya (hereafter “IMPRODATWRM”) is expected to be designed to close the institutional and information-management gap while strengthening WRA's own-source revenue base and the evidence available for sustainable allocation. The Assignment is to support WRA in transforming its fragmented digital landscape into an integrated, interoperable WRIMS environment that connects the full operating chain - from registration and permitting through meter/device management, reliable measurement, validation, billing, payment reconciliation, inspection and enforcement, and will connect these regulatory transactions to basin-level hydrological information. Shared identifiers, GIS references, data-governance rules and interoperable interfaces are essential across this chain.
